implementation_notes: No class is generated: __getattr__ is called only for attributes the proxy does not define, so a single hook forwards the whole surface, while __setattr__/__delattr__ (or __getattribute__ when total interception is required) route mutation and __class__/__dir__ are spoofed when isinstance-style transparency is needed. That protocol hook replaces the per-class proxy, and its limit is that the interpreter resolves special methods on the type, so len(), iteration, arithmetic, context managers and awaitables must be declared on the proxy class itself.
pitfalls: Dunder lookups bypass __getattr__: len(proxy), for x in proxy, with proxy and the operators silently fail unless the proxy class defines the dunders.
__getattr__ calling itself recurses when it touches its own attributes before they exist; keep state in object.__setattr__ or a private mapping.
Spoofing __class__ makes isinstance() report the target while copy, pickle and static type checkers keep seeing the proxy class.
weakref.proxy dies with its target, so a proxy used as a long-lived cache key or callback must hold a strong reference deliberately.

variants.name: wrapt.ObjectProxy transparent proxy
variants.implementation_notes: wrapt ships a C-extension transparent object proxy that already implements the special methods, so a custom proxy derives from ObjectProxy and overrides only what it intercepts; FunctionWrapper handles the descriptor and bound-method case that hand-written proxies get wrong. Choose it when the proxy must behave like the wrapped object across operators and callables, at the cost of a third-party dependency and a new class per proxied shape.
pitfalls: ObjectProxy deliberately omits __call__, iterator and awaitable methods, so a callable target needs CallableObjectProxy or an explicit override.
AutoObjectProxy and LazyObjectProxy create a class per instance, so memory grows with proxy count; use them only when lazy or dynamic behaviour demands it.

variants.name: spec-derived test double
variants.implementation_notes: create_autospec inspects the target at run time and builds a stand-in whose members and signatures match, which is the test-double realization of the same decision: the double is derived from the real object instead of written per class. Mock(wraps=...) records every call while delegating to the target, so both stubbing and interaction verification come from one runtime-generated object.
variants.code_sketch:
from unittest import mock

service = mock.create_autospec(PaymentService, instance=True)  # members and signatures from the class
service.charge("order-1")
service.charge.assert_called_once_with("order-1")

recorder = mock.Mock(wraps=real_service)                        # forwards and records
pitfalls: Without autospec a Mock accepts any attribute and any signature, so typos and wrong arity pass the test suite instead of failing it.
Mock is not a type: isinstance and type checks see Mock, and spec_set must be used to reject attributes the target does not declare.
